newsitem.title: Italy: Bertinotti warns Italy coalition over welfare plan.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti warns Italy coalition over welfare plan.

text.p: Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti said on Tuesday that a meeting of political forces supporting Prime Minister Romano Prodi's majority had not resolved differences over Italy's three-year economic plan, particularly aspects affecting the welfare state.
"The differences remain," Bertinotti said in a statement.
"As things stand the Communist Refoundation Party cannot give its consent," his statement said.

Bertinotti, on whose party Prodi relies for its majority in the lower house of parliament, said that the plan did not sufficiently tackle the problems of unemployment, the poorer south and the need to crack down on tax evasion.

The leader of the Marxist party said that with the current outline of the three-year plan, known as the DPEF, the government was "bowing to a monetarist reading" of the Maastricht treaty on European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
During the meeting, which ended after midnight, Bertinotti held his ground that his party was against welfare spending cuts, particularly on pensions and health care.
He said in the statement that Refoundation remained opposed to government proposals to enact changes to Italy's costly pensions system starting from next year.
Bertinotti, however, did not totally close the door on an eventual compromise with the government.
"It is still to be hoped that there can be positive changes in the orientation of the government, for which we, in any case, will continue to fight," he said.
Participants said the meeting was not polemical and neither Bertinotti nor other political leaders had issued ultimatums.

The strategy, known as the economic and financial planning document (DPEF), will outline how the government intends to cut another 25 trillion lire ($15 billion) from the public deficit in the 1998 budget.
Italian radio said Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told the meeting that the proposed 1998 budget would be made up of about two-thirds spending cuts and one-third new revenues.
Massimo D'Alema, leader of the Democratic Party of the Left (PDS), the largest force in Prodi's coalition, told reporters after the meeting that there was "no doubt" that the DPEF would be approved.
The plan is expected to be the subject of a cabinet meeting this week, most likely on Friday.
The DPEF is a crucial part of Italy's plans for stabilising state finances and keeping alive hopes of joining European economic and monetary union by the planned 1999 start date.
